1i6ip9e:208: The measured 169x GDS speedup comes from three combined optimizations: ① pre-sharding removes all-gather overhead; ② pre-quantization (BF16→FP8) halves the data volume; ③ parallel GDS direct-to-HBM transfer eliminates the bounce buffer. Doing only ③ would significantly narrow the gains—vLLM V1 has already removed some bottlenecks with parallel loading, but CPU-side serialization/quantization still dominates. This means offline preparation (pre-shard + pre-quantize) is a necessary prerequisite for this approach and cannot be skipped.
1kpqom8:253: In the traditional CPU-based loading path, data flows through four hops: "storage → CPU memory → PCIe → GPU HBM", and the CPU bounce buffer is the hardest bottleneck to eliminate—every GPU read requires a memory copy and deserialization on the CPU side. The core value of GDS is not saturating the 94 GiB/s throughput, but compressing this path to two hops, "storage → GPU HBM", completely removing CPU involvement. For a 405B model, this means 8 GPUs can truly read from their respective shards in parallel without queuing for CPU scheduling.
